statement: Domaine Houillon is the southern Rhône estate of Aurélien and Charlotte Houillon at Faucon, with a 2017 first vintage and about 4.5 hectares of vines within a larger nine-hectare holding.

Vine Trail describes Domaine Houillon as certified organic by Ecocert and practising biodynamic farming; CARTA records the certification as source-attributed and does not infer a separate biodynamic certification.
scope_notes: No certificate record was independently acquired in Run 09.

statement: Aurélien Houillon is the brother of Emmanuel Houillon and Adeline Houillon; the siblings share an Overnoy lineage but Domaine Houillon, Maison Pierre Overnoy / Emmanuel Houillon, and Renaud Bruyère & Adeline Houillon are separate producer identities.
Vine Trail reports that Aurélien Houillon learned and worked alongside Pierre Overnoy in the Jura from 2007 to 2013 before later creating Domaine Houillon in the southern Rhône.
Canne is a durable Domaine Houillon red cuvée whose name refers to the tap used for free-run juice; the wine is made as pure jus de goutte while the press fraction goes to another cuvée.
For 2021, Vine Trail documents Canne as 70% Grenache and 30% Syrah, 13.5% alcohol, from 50–60-year-old vines after roughly ten weeks of cuvaison.
Trade evidence for 2022 describes Canne as 100% Grenache and Vin de France with a 65-day maceration; this is retained provisionally pending producer or bottle-level confirmation.
resolution_needed: Verify the 2022 bottle or producer technical sheet before closing composition and legal category.

statement: Burgess Cellars was founded by Tom Burgess in 1972 and was acquired in 2020 by the Lawrence family / Lawrence Wine Estates; CARTA keeps the historic Burgess producer identity continuous across that ownership transition.
Promiscua is a Burgess Cellars Cabernet Sauvignon cuvée, first released from the 2021 vintage, and is not a separate producer or label entity.
For 2021, the producer documents Promiscua as 100% Cabernet Sauvignon, fermented with native yeast via pied de cuve and aged 22 months in French oak, 20% new and 80% neutral.
Current producer material labels Promiscua as Napa Valley and documents the 2022 release as 100% Cabernet Sauvignon sourced from Burgess single vineyards.

The 2021 inaugural Promiscua is attributed to Meghan Zobeck, while Reid Griggs joined Lawrence Wine Estates in 2023 and is the current Burgess winemaker; CARTA therefore time-scopes winemaker roles instead of treating the attributions as contradictory.

Natus Vini is Hamilton Reis's family wine project at Monte Natus near Vidigueira; Intus is a wine line within Natus Vini, not a separate producer, and the line uses stainless steel throughout vinification and ageing.
Trade technical material identifies Intus Tinto as a blend of Trincadeira and Aragonez; CARTA governs Aragonez on the existing Tempranillo grape identity.
The Intus wines are represented in trade as Vinho Regional Alentejano, corresponding to the Alentejano protected geographical indication rather than a Vidigueira DOC identity.
The regional wine commission places Natus Vini at Monte Natus in Vidigueira, Alentejo.

The Bébian seed resolves to Tartuguier, not 'Tartuguière'; Tartuguier is a Prieuré Saint-Jean de Bébian red cuvée and the near-identical Château Tartuguière name belongs to an unrelated Bordeaux estate.

Tartuguier is documented as a watercourse at Pézenas; CARTA represents the hydronym as a geographic feature and does not infer a vineyard, cadastral parcel, ownership geometry, or appellation containment from the cuvée name.

For 2022, a distributor technical lineage gives Tartuguier as 70% Mourvèdre and 30% Grenache, while a merchant description gives approximately 80% Mourvèdre and 20% Grenache; CARTA preserves the material discrepancy and prefers neither as exact machine truth.
resolution_needed: Seek producer or bottle-level 2022 composition authority.

statement: Tartuguier is documented as Vin de France for the 2021–2023 parcel-cuvée period reviewed in Run 09; CARTA does not infer a Languedoc or Pézenas designation from the estate's physical location.
Agence Bio records Prieuré Saint-Jean de Bébian under Ecocert France with organic engagement dated 2015-04-23; CARTA does not infer biodynamic certification from trade descriptions.
Williams Corner Wine lists Prieuré Saint-Jean de Bébian in its current U.S. grower portfolio.

Domaine Carrel & Senger is the continuous producer/legal person formerly presented as Domaine Eugène Carrel & Fils; the 2022 transition brought Thomas Senger into management while Olivier Carrel remained associated with the same enterprise.

Jongieux Blanc is a Jacquère white wine under the Vin de Savoie / Savoie geographic denomination Jongieux; the producer product page names Jacquère and the official appellation rules make Jacquère the principal white variety for Jongieux.

The producer shop index's Chardonnay tag/slug for Jongieux Blanc is rejected as a CMS taxonomy artifact because the product page identifies Jacquère and the Jongieux legal framework centers Jacquère for white wine.

VIVC lists 'Roussette' among names for Jacquère while also listing Roussette-family names for Altesse; CARTA must not merge Jacquère and Altesse on the shared string, and Roussette de Savoie remains an Altesse appellation context.
Williams Corner Wine lists the Carrel producer world in its current U.S. grower portfolio.

French registry and organic-operator records use DOMAINE LAMPYRES as the legal producer name for François-Xavier Dauré; Domaine des Lampyres and Les Lampyres are retained as sourced trade-name variants rather than duplicate producers.
Domaine Lampyres works from Espira-de-l'Agly in Roussillon while the registered company seat is in Rivesaltes; CARTA keeps cellar geography distinct from the administrative registered address.

Agence Bio records Domaine Lampyres under Ecocert France with engagement dated 2017-08-07; current records also include wine-grape land in conversion, so CARTA does not back-project certification to the 2016 or 2017 wines.

For 2023, Harvest Moon is documented as Vin de France, 50% Grenache and 50% Mourvèdre from a neighbouring organic grower's vineyard, co-fermented with destemmed Grenache and whole-cluster Mourvèdre and aged three months in stainless steel.

For 2024, Harvest Moon is documented as Vin de France, 90% Grenache and 10% Mourvèdre with five days of co-fermentation and six months in stainless steel and fibreglass; the large blend and cellar change remains attached to the same persistent wine identity.

Independent specialist reporting states that François-Xavier Dauré joined Tom Lubbe at Domaine Matassa in 2015 and worked there for five vintages while developing his own project; the relationship is retained as work-line context without activating a new Matassa producer node in this pass.
Terres Blanches supplies current U.S. importer technical material for Harvest Moon in the 2023 and 2024 vintages.

Vindiou is a 2020 wine-producing business founded and managed by Thomas Junique and Cyprien De Lageneste at Plats, Ardèche; its registered activities include purchasing grapes for vinification as well as viticulture, so CARTA does not flatten it into either pure négoce or pure estate farming.

For 2024, Cœur Fidèle is documented as a 100% Dureza Vin de France from a Dureza plot planted in 2020 on sand over granitic subsoil, with organic farming claimed, five days of whole-bunch maceration and eight months in used barrels.

Peer-reviewed grape-genetics work identifies Dureza as one parent of Syrah, with Mondeuse Blanche as the other parent; CARTA records the direct Dureza-to-Syrah genetic relationship and does not infer stylistic similarity from that pedigree.

Current importer material describes Domaine Numa Cornut as a Burgundy estate founded in 2020 with approximately 4.5 hectares of leased and owned vineyards across the Côte de Beaune and Côte de Nuits; this narrows the earlier Run 09C estate-versus-négoce uncertainty without asserting that all parcels are owned.
Numa Cornut comes from the Château Guiot winegrowing family in the southern Rhône but his Burgundy producer world is a distinct project and must not be merged with Château Guiot.

Distributor material documents the 2023 Numa Cornut Aligoté as 100% Aligoté, 12.5% alcohol, from clay-limestone fruit described as mostly from the Meursault area, partly fermented in oak and matured about ten months in cask.

The distributor product record calls the wine simply 'Grand vin de Bourgogne — Aligoté', while multiple retailers use 'Vieilles Vignes Bourgogne Aligoté'; CARTA therefore keeps 'Vieilles Vignes' as a provisional name form and does not infer a defined old-vine age.
resolution_needed: Confirm a bottle/label or producer record showing whether Vieilles Vignes is part of the official wine name.

statement: The seed wine belongs to the Bourgogne Aligoté AOC; CARTA keeps the regional appellation distinct from the report's physical fruit-source description near Meursault.

VIVC treats Grenache and Grenache Noir as names for the Garnacha Tinta grape identity; CARTA therefore reuses the existing Garnacha Tinta node for the French Grenache fruit in Run 09 rather than creating a duplicate grape.
Aragonez is a governed Portuguese name for the Tempranillo grape identity and is the label/trade name used for the Intus Tinto component in this run.
VIVC governs Trincadeira and Tinta Amarela as names of the same grape identity; CARTA uses Trincadeira as the canonical node for the Intus Tinto component.

The best additional Run 09 evidence lists the 2018 Anika Grenache as Santa Barbara County, but that value remains merchant-tier and has not been verified against a TTB COLA or bottle image; the exact labeled appellation therefore remains provisional.
resolution_needed: Confirm with TTB COLA or bottle/back-label authority.

statement: François Blanchard's first-party Le Grand-Cléré page describes the single 2.74-hectare parcel as controlled by Ecocert SAS; this materially strengthens the certification-control claim but does not establish a certificate number or certification start date.
resolution_needed: Certificate number and exact certification dates remain open.

statement: The German Wine Institute states that every Qualitätswein and Prädikatswein that passes required testing receives an Amtliche Prüfungsnummer that must appear on the label; the 2018 source wording 'No AP' therefore supports that this bottling was not presented as Qualitätswein or Prädikatswein, while the exact lower legal tier remains unresolved.
resolution_needed: Do not choose Landwein versus Deutscher Wein without bottle or producer authority.

statement: Vine Trail presents the 2021 Canne release as Côtes-du-Rhône; CARTA scopes that designation to the documented vintage rather than treating it as timeless.
Demeine Estates presents Burgess in its current winery portfolio and sales/marketing platform.
